findings.title: New in R2: §3.7's drift rule and §3.6's fresh-pair resume rule give opposite instructions at the reconnect boundary, and drift can never be cleared by re-alignment
findings.detail: The two R1 remediations collide. §3.7 says that once external session drift is detected the coordinator must not push settings back — 'router可继续依native实际设置工作，标source=external_session_settings，不得附旧registry pair把人的选择盖回' — and that drift clears only via '后续新显式set（即使desired内容相同也生成新configGeneration）'. §3.6 says the opposite for bootstrap: '冷启动、监督器重连、thread rotation均在各自 ensureThread 内新读已验证registry，按这一个generation构建model+effort' and 'start/resume每次调用都用fresh模型设置…决不能先传旧env再等后台reconcile修正'. Failure scenario: hot set puts effort=high and status reads observed; the founder types /model in the TUI and drops to low; §3.7 marks effectiveStatus=drifted and stops pushing; the app-server child is then respawned by the supervisor; §3.6's ensureThread resumes with the fresh registry pair, so the runtime is silently back at high — i.e. the founder's choice IS overwritten, which §3.7 forbids — while status still reads drifted, because only an explicit set clears it. The operator now sees drifted on a runtime that is actually aligned, and B7 ('已observed后在TUI改effort，registry保持原值 → 当前状态drifted、真实轮次用TUI值且无自动覆盖') does not cover a reconnect, so the contradiction is untested. The plan needs an explicit precedence rule at the bootstrap boundary (registry wins at ensureThread; founder wins mid-session) plus a drift-clearing condition on observed re-alignment, and a B7 variant that reconnects while drifted.

findings.title: New in R2: §3.7 puts readRuntimeConfig on every router turn's preflight without specifying failure behavior or a latency budget
findings.detail: §3.7 promotes readRuntimeConfig from a declared socket capability (§3.3) to a load-bearing per-turn call: 'readRuntimeConfig在status请求、router preflight和5秒reconcile时读current pair，与source一起校验；不能仅看registry digest.' That is a thread/read RPC (codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs:654; the returned ThreadSettings carries model and effort at v2/thread.rs:284,287, so the read itself is well-founded) now sitting in front of the Lead's main work path. The plan states no behavior when it fails or hangs. §3.3's fail-closed rule is scoped to registry/summary invalidity ('当前 registry 文件或 summary无效时，不应用…status=unavailable'), and §3.5's runtime_hot_config_unsupported covers the stage path — neither covers a transient runtime read error at router preflight. Failure scenario: the app-server is briefly busy or the socket read times out during preflight; a fail-closed implementation blocks router admission and the Lead stops answering the founder over an advisory config read, violating §3.5's 'not touching the process supervisor / not interrupting turns' spirit; a fail-open implementation silently degrades to registry-digest-only checking, which §3.7 explicitly forbids. Every other wait in the design has a number (10s apply, 5s reconcile); this one has none. Specify the timeout, the disposition on failure, and whether preflight is advisory or blocking.

findings.title: New in R2: T3 now refactors lead-registry.ts, but the precise test entrypoints run none of its six existing suites
findings.detail: The M3 remediation replaced the new scripts/lead-config-write.mjs with '复用/小范围提取 packages/flywheel-comm/src/commands/lead-registry.ts 的 no-follow、writeAtomic、fsyncDirectory 原语到 lead-registry-file-io.ts（新增导出入口）'. That extracts private helpers out of the module that fences summary-receipt-verified registry writes — writeAtomic()+fsyncDirectory() at lead-registry.ts:121-133 and the readRegularFileNoFollow + FLYWHEEL_SUMMARY_CONFIG_LOCK_HELD sentinel at :604-620 (also :928, :1097). Those helpers have no direct unit test: grepping packages/flywheel-comm/src/__tests__/ for writeAtomic / readRegularFileNoFollow / fsyncDirectory returns nothing; their only regression guard is the six command-level suites (lead-registry-add, -cli, -cos-context, -cos-context-cli, -recover, -verifier, ~1900 lines total). The '精确测试入口' block runs only workflow-template-cli.test.ts, lead-config-cli.test.ts and summary-registry-migration.test.ts on the comm side, so a botched extraction — e.g. dropping the fsync of the containing directory, or losing the no-follow re-open before the CAS — ships green. Add the lead-registry-* suites to the comm test entrypoint line; T3 also correctly notes '改其package导出', which is required because packages/flywheel-comm/package.json exports is an explicit allowlist with no wildcard.

findings.title: New in R2: T1 lists workflow-menu.ts in the evidence column instead of the '精确文件' column implementers scope from
findings.detail: The M4 remediation correctly threads one modelSnapshot through the seed compile chain (§2.3 now names loadWorkflowMenuSeeds, loadWorkflowMenuLibrary/menuFromGraph, compileWorkflowMenuSeed and all resolveAlias call sites, which matches the ambient-fallback defaults at workflow-menu.ts:233-235 and the snapshot-less calls at :279,:280,:306). But in the T1 row the string '改 workflow-menu.ts 传入单个modelSnapshot' landed in the third column ('测试与完成证据'), not the second ('精确文件'), where every other touched file is listed — StateStore.ts, management-dag-writer.ts, management-existing-writers.ts. Given §4's own rule '只改列明链路', an implementer scoping strictly from column 2 would omit the one file the fix depends on. Move it to column 2.

findings.title: New in R2: §3.6's build-identity gate says 'same payload' but the launcher and the generator reach production through two different distribution mechanisms
findings.detail: §3.6 gates the hot capability on 'stage必须验证当前carrier能力包含这套bootstrap contract版本 registry_tuning_v1，并核部署artifact build identity（包括canonical launcher+generator属于同一payload）'. The gate is the right idea — it is what prevents a hot write from landing against an old launcher that still carries the removed assert — but 'payload' is ambiguous here because the two artifacts are delivered differently. The Codex TUI launchers and scripts/flywheel-daemon.sh execute out of the repo checkout: ~/.flywheel/bin/flywheel-codex-lead-wrapper-mufasa-tui-fullaccess.sh hardcodes MAIN_REPO=/Users/xiaorongli/Dev/flywheel and sources ${MAIN_REPO}/packages/teamlead/scripts/..., and flywheel-daemon.sh has no installed copy under ~/.flywheel/bin at all. But Raya — the plan's named target — launches via ProgramArguments /Users/xiaorongli/.flywheel/bin/flywheel-lead.sh, a *copied* artifact installed by scripts/package-onboard.sh. Today that copy is byte-identical to the repo (both sha256 67854652194ea3bc16104da2ae9e5b7ea3eb9b768fbd3573f3587eccca11c713) so there is no live drift, and flywheel-lead.sh:200-208 already unsets FLYWHEEL_LEAD_MODEL/EFFORT/MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOW before the Codex launcher — so Raya is doubly safe. Still, the gate should say it verifies the bytes the *next launch will source*, naming both roots, rather than a single build identity; otherwise a future divergence between the packaged bin and the repo silently weakens the only thing standing between a hot write and the R1 brick.
